correctness.rationale: For every eleven-adic input the falling-factorial series is one-Lipschitz and locally analytic. Integer-jet coefficients truncated at term 32 give the complete mod-eleven branch certificate (eight unit derivatives, three zero derivatives with invertible second coefficient). Eight branches are exact isometries. Each singular branch has a unique critical center and a global quadratic normal form from a restricted-analytic square-root coordinate. The square-root formula counts every prime-power fiber, and the parity split yields the actual derangement counts. The independent recurrence-based enumerator matched all 11+121+1331+14641+161051+1771561 target residues at the first six powers. Infinite correctness rests on the normal-form argument, not on the finite tests; the eleven-adic constants are algorithmically defined and no numerical approximation is treated as proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete, motivated number-theoretic invariant of the classical derangement sequence: all residues and multiplicities modulo all powers of the first odd prime beyond three with quadratic critical branches. It reveals exactly seven attained residue balls of Haar measure 7/11, together with unbounded singular fiber multiplicities that distinguish the prime eleven from regular primes five and seven. These are exact natural invariants with a structural lifting explanation and reusable modular-counting consequences; they are not a small ad hoc finite table.
